proofs.full_local_argument:
LOCAL ARGUMENT; NOT SOURCE TEXT. Write α=1-p. Let Hk=σ(ξ0,B0,...,ξk-1,Bk-1), with H0 trivial, and Jk=Hk∨σ(ξk). The variables zk,wk,bk,yk are Hk-measurable; xk=zk+1 and vk are Jk-measurable. Bk is independent of Jk and has mean p. Conditional expectations below always use these complete histories, never a filtration containing the fresh ξk before its sampling. Put Δk=Fξk(yk)-Fξk(wk) and δk=vk-F(yk)=Δk-[F(yk)-F(wk)]. Independence, unbiasedness and the same-sample difference give E[δk|Hk]=0 and E[||δk||²|Hk]<=E[||Δk||²|Hk]<=L²||yk-wk||². The centered expression has +F(wk), not the source's printed second minus sign. Jensen also gives ||F(u)-F(v)||<=L||u-v|| on D.

All iterates lie in D because proximal minimizers have finite g, and D is convex. The proximal optimality relation is (a-q)/τ∈∂g(q) for q=prox_{τg}(a), hence <q-a,z-q>>=τ[g(q)-g(z)]. Existence follows because a proper closed convex function has an affine minorant, so adding the positive quadratic gives a coercive strictly convex objective. The same optimality relation for two proximal points, added in opposite directions, gives their nonexpansiveness. Consequently finite second moments of zk,wk imply those of yk and xk: F is Lipschitz on D, the difference Δk has the displayed conditional second-moment bound, and a proximal map has at most affine growth relative to any fixed input. Starting from deterministic z0,w0, induction proves finite second moments at every finite horizon. For a fixed z∈D, the proximal inequality bounds g(q) above by g(z)+<q-a,z-q>/τ, whose absolute value has finite expectation at these inputs; an affine minorant bounds g(q) below by an integrable affine function. Thus all g-values, inner products and errors used below are integrable. On compact C, F is bounded and g has a finite lower bound, so the comparison maxima have integrable upper bounds; fixing any point of C gives integrable lower bounds. Suprema of the affine-in-output comparison terms are lower semicontinuous functions of that output and hence measurable. Their maxima in z exist because F is continuous on D and -g is upper semicontinuous on C.

For readability suppress k inside an iteration and write b=αzk+pwk, y=yk, x=xk, w=wk and v=vk. Apply proximal optimality to x=prox_{τg}(b-τv) with comparator z∈D and to y=prox_{τg}(b-τF(w)) with comparator x. Adding gives
τ[g(y)-g(z)] <= <x-b,z-x>+<y-b,x-y>+τ<v,z-y>+τ<F(w)-v,x-y>.
Expanding the first two inner products gives exactly
2<x-b,z-x>+2<y-b,x-y> = α||zk-z||²+p||w-z||²-||x-z||²-α||y-zk||²-p||y-w||²-||x-y||².
Since F(w)-v=-Δk, defining Θk(z)=<F(y),y-z>+g(y)-g(z) and e1k(z)=2τ<δk,z-y> yields
2τΘk(z)+||x-z||² <= α||zk-z||²+p||w-z||²-p||y-w||²-||x-y||²+2τ<-Δk,x-y>+e1k(z),
where the nonpositive term -α||y-zk||² has been dropped.

Define Φk(z)=α||zk-z||²+||wk-z||², Ak=||yk-wk||², Dk=||xk-yk||², and
e2k(z)=p||wk-z||²+||wk+1-z||²-||wk-z||²-p||xk-z||².
Adding the change of snapshot norm to the preceding inequality gives the pathwise estimate
2τΘk(z)+Φk+1(z) <= Φk(z)-pAk-Dk+2τ<-Δk,xk-yk>+e1k(z)+e2k(z). (L1)
Here e2k(z)=2<dk,z>+ck with dk=pxk+(1-p)wk-wk+1 and ck=||wk+1||²-p||xk||²-(1-p)||wk||². The Bernoulli law gives E[dk|Jk]=0, E[ck|Jk]=0 and E[||dk||²|Jk]=p(1-p)||xk-wk||². In particular dk has conditional mean zero given Hk.

Young's inequality and τ²L²=γ²p imply
E[2τ<-Δk,xk-yk>|Hk] <= γ E[Dk|Hk]+(τ²/γ)E[||Δk||²|Hk] <= γ E[Dk|Hk]+γpAk. (L2)
For s∈C∩Sol, monotonicity and the solution inequality give Θk(s)>=<F(s),yk-s>+g(yk)-g(s)>=0. For this fixed s, E[e1k(s)|Hk]=0 because yk is Hk-measurable, and E[e2k(s)|Hk]=0 by the tower property. Taking conditional expectation in (L1), applying (L2), and summing therefore yields
Σ_{k<K} E[pAk+Dk] <= Φ0(s)/(1-γ). (L3)
No assumption that an arbitrary compact C controls a solution radius has been used: s was explicitly chosen in C∩Sol.

We next prove the comparison-maximum estimate rather than assume an external lemma. If uk is Hk+1-measurable, square integrable and E[uk|Hk]=0, set X0=z0 and Xk+1=Xk+uk. Expanding squared norms gives
Σ_{k<K}<uk,z> = (||z0-z||²-||XK-z||²)/2 + (1/2)Σ_{k<K}||uk||² + Σ_{k<K}<uk,Xk>.
The last sum has expectation zero since Xk is Hk-measurable and square integrable. Drop the negative final norm and maximize over C to obtain
E max_{z∈C}Σ_{k<K}<uk,z> <= R_C²/2+(1/2)Σ_{k<K}E||uk||². (L4)
For uk=2τδk, the subtracted term Σ<uk,yk> in Σe1k has expectation zero. Thus (L4) gives
E max_C Σe1k(z) <= R_C²/2+2τ²L²Σ E Ak. (L5)
For uk=dk, the z-independent Σck in Σe2k has expectation zero. Apply twice (L4) and use the Bernoulli variance identity to get
E max_C Σe2k(z) <= R_C²+p(1-p)Σ E||xk-wk||². (L6)
These applications use the same complete Hk; the stronger conditional zero mean of dk given Jk justifies the refresh calculation even though xk depends on ξk.

For every z∈C, monotonicity gives <F(z),yk-z><=<F(yk),yk-z>. Convexity gives Kg(zbarK)<=Σg(yk). Consequently K Gap_C(zbarK)<=max_C ΣΘk(z). Sum (L1), discard -ΦK(z), take the comparison maximum and expectation, and use (L2) to discard the nonpositive expected sum of -pAk-Dk and the cross term. Using max(a+b)<=max a+max b and (L5),(L6), this yields
2τK E Gap_C(zbarK) <= max_C Φ0(z)+(3/2)R_C²+Σ E[2τ²L²Ak+p(1-p)||xk-wk||²]. (L7)
To bound the final sum, use τ²L²<=p and write a=yk-wk, b=xk-yk. Young's inequality with t=√2-1 gives ||a+b||²<=(1+t)||a||²+(1+1/t)||b||²=√2||a||²+(2+√2)||b||². Therefore
2τ²L²Ak+p(1-p)||xk-wk||² <= p[2Ak+||a+b||²] <= (2+√2)(pAk+pDk) <= 3.5(pAk+Dk).
By (L3), its summed expectation is at most 3.5 Φ0(s)/(1-γ). Since w0=z0, Φ0(z)=(2-p)||z0-z||². The explicit containment s∈C implies Φ0(s)<=max_C Φ0=(2-p)R_C²<=2R_C². Substitute these inequalities in (L7) to obtain
2τK E Gap_C(zbarK) <= [2+3/2+7/(1-γ)]R_C² =7[1/2+1/(1-γ)]R_C².
Dividing by 2τK and substituting τ=γ√p/L proves the stated bound. At γ=1/2 the coefficient is 17.5L/(√p K). The construction also covers p=1: α=0 and the same inequalities remain valid. If R_C=0, (L7) and the preceding energy bound still apply without division by R_C.

Finally run the stated deterministic K for ε>0. There are exactly 2K stochastic evaluations and 2K proximal evaluations. Initializing the snapshot costs one full F; each Bernoulli refresh costs at most one further full F, so expected charged stochastic-evaluation units are at most N+(2+pN)K. The possibly unused terminal refresh may be omitted. For N>=2, p=2/N is admissible, 2+pN=4, and K<=1+17.5 L R_C²/(√p ε), giving N+4+70√(N/2)L R_C²/ε=O(N+√N L R_C²/ε). This proves only the selected Algorithm's expected cost under the stated cost convention; no inference about other Algorithms or unrestricted Oracle Complexity is made.

assumptions: g:Z→R∪{+∞} is proper convex lower semicontinuous; its proximal operator is evaluated exactly. F:D→Z is monotone and Sol is nonempty.

The measurable stochastic oracle has E_Q Fξ(z)=F(z) for every z∈D and E_Q||Fξ(u)-Fξ(v)||²<=L²||u-v||² for every u,v∈D. The same ξ is used at both points of each difference. Each ξk has distribution Q independently of the complete past. All evaluated random maps and resulting iterates are measurable.

C is deterministic, nonempty, compact, contained in D, and contains at least one s∈Sol. This is an explicit local strengthening of the source's compact-C wording. It guarantees Φ0(s)<=max_C Φ0, rather than inferring this inequality from compactness alone.

Use Algorithm 1 with deterministic z0=w0∈D, exact snapshots F(wk), α=1-p and τ=γ√p/L. At iteration k set bk=αzk+pwk, yk=prox_{τg}(bk-τF(wk)), vk=F(wk)+Fξk(yk)-Fξk(wk), zk+1=prox_{τg}(bk-τvk). After computing zk+1, draw an independent Bernoulli(p) variable Bk and set wk+1=zk+1 if Bk=1 and wk otherwise.
statement.conclusion: E[Gap_C(zbarK)] <= [7L/(2γ√p K)](1/2+1/(1-γ))R_C². In particular γ=1/2 gives E[Gap_C(zbarK)]<=17.5 L R_C²/(√p K). Thus K=max{1,ceil(17.5 L R_C²/(√p ε))} suffices at γ=1/2. If one exact F costs N stochastic-evaluation units, expected charged evaluations are at most N+(2+pN)K, including initialization and allowing a terminal refresh charge; additionally charge 2K exact proximal evaluations. With N>=2 and p=2/N this is O(N+√N L R_C²/ε) expected charged evaluations. These are selected-Algorithm upper bounds, not unrestricted Oracle Complexity claims.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Z is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. D=dom g={z:g(z)<+∞}. Sol={s∈D:<F(s),z-s>+g(z)-g(s)>=0 for every z∈D}. Fix a deterministic nonempty compact C⊂D with C∩Sol nonempty. For w∈D define Gap_C(w)=max_{z∈C}{<F(z),w-z>+g(w)-g(z)} and R_C²=max_{z∈C}||z0-z||². C need not be convex; the output average belongs to the convex set D. This maximum is taken on C itself, not on a possibly noncompact C∩D. The assumptions below make F Lipschitz on D, so the comparison expression is upper semicontinuous in z on compact C and attains a finite maximum.
statement.parameter_domains: L>0; p∈(0,1]; γ∈(0,1); α=1-p; τ=γ√p/L; K>=1 integer. For an accuracy target ε>0 use the tuning specified in the conclusion. The finite-sum resource specialization assumes full F costs N stochastic-evaluation units, with integer N>=2 for p=2/N.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every data set satisfying these assumptions, every deterministic feasible initialization, every such C, every p∈(0,1], γ∈(0,1), and every integer K>=1, let zbarK=K^{-1}Σ_{k=0}^{K-1}yk. The bound concerns E[Gap_C(zbarK)], with expectation over all ξk and Bk. It is an expectation of a maximum and a guarantee for the half-step average. No last-iterate statement is asserted.
